metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The universe or nature itself feels empathy and responds with deep sorrow to human suffering.
acceptable_visual_variants: A vast, dark sky filled with heavy, low-hanging clouds that seem to envelop a weeping figure.
A twilight sky with soft, drooping mist or fog settling gently around a person in distress.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: The physical sky bends down physically in response to someone's pain.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might draw a literal blue sky physically curving or drooping down like a piece of fabric, which looks cartoonish and misses the emotional depth of cosmic empathy.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The gender-neutral pronoun 'उसने' (Usne) is translated as 'She', which resolves the original Hindi's deliberate gender ambiguity to a specific female subject.
The rhythmic flow and internal rhyme of 'samjho' (understand) and 'jhukta hai' (bends) are lost in the English prose structure.

original_poem:
उसने कहा था कि दर्द को समझो,  
कि जब कोई रोता है तो आकाश भी उसकी पीड़ा में झुकता है।  
उसने कहा था कि घावों के भीतर छुपे हैं अनगिनत फूल,  
जो खिलने का इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।  

उसने कहा था कि कभी किसी के आंसूओं को हल्के में मत लेना,  
क्योंकि हर आंसू की एक कहानी होती है।  
उसने कहा था कि प्रेम सिर्फ़ एक शब्द नहीं,  
यह एक दुनिया है, जिसमें बसी है सच्चाई और करुणा।  

उसने कहा था कि कभी मत भूलना  
कि एक इंसान की आत्मा कितनी नाज़ुक होती है,  
और जब हम उस पर चोट करते हैं,  
तो हम खुद अपने वजूद को भी चोट पहुँचाते हैं।
translated_poem:
She had said to understand the pain,  
that when someone cries, the sky also bends in their sorrow.  
She had said that countless flowers lie hidden in wounds,  
waiting to bloom.  

She had said to never take someone’s tears lightly,  
for each tear has a story.  
She had said that love is not just a word,  
it’s a world where truth and compassion reside.  

She had said to never forget  
how delicate a person’s soul can be,  
and when we hurt them,  
we wound our own being as well.
